This is a message I sent during a conversation with my boy who doesn't trade, I was saying how I had to come to terms with reality and how I’ve been facing my emotions instead of letting them hold me back, then he asked me what I was dealing with and this was my response - Not really dealing with shit but I just let my emotions dictate my decisions too much when I’m on the charts, had a small crash out over a small loss that shouldn’t have mattered as much as it did, but I’m glad that I made it matter so much cus it opened up my blind eye, I’ve always had trouble being impatient and letting my anger get the best of me at certain times and the chart was just my biggest reflection of that, I already tried everything else to get my psychology down but the only thing I didn’t try was putting down the za, so I took the rest of the week off, finished the last bit of za I had and just haven’t looked back since, started filming psychology videos of me just talking to myself and listing all my flaws that I’ve been running away from and it’s just made me calmer overall in and out of the charts, I think the za was just too easy of dopamine for me and it made me chase/force trades to find more easy dopamine which just made me trickle down my profits, small loss by small loss then I guess that day was just the straw that broke the camels back, then i decided enough was enough (edited)

Emotional Analysis
Noticed that my mind was very indecisive during the session. I had 3 different strategies lined up in my head at the same time and that probably was giving me a lot of trouble. And i'm not sure if I was getting impatient or something, but i decided the jump onto the nearest good looking trade off of impulse. Think I was seeing others typing that they already got a trade W and felt fomo or rushed to get a trade in. Not even 30 mins in i was impulsed to take a trade. That certainly is where an issue lies. Within the trade, price did bounce a bit, and i was quickly stopped. The thing i totally disregarded and was probably most important, seeing the 'tomorrow's capital' from today's trade. I blew one account. If I knew that would be a result of a bad trade, losing the opportunity of a 5k payout account, I would be much more cautious. but instead, i found myself in this hunting mode for trades, not really aware of consequences, at that point it was just will i win this trade or no. Not much thought on probabilities, just fomo'ing in. 

Post loss, the levels that Rich highlighted got tapped in and won. 4R to 5R. That part tilted me. In my head, if i just waited for that moment, i would have won the trade. But why didn't I take his levels and go for the lowest hanging fruit? FOMO for sure. The win I did have is that I did not take another trade. This usually would tilt the shit out of me, but I accept the loss and the lost account for this opportunity to learn. As these losses bring me closer to more wins and profits. Biggest lesson here, FOMO is still an issue, patience still needs to be worked on, and indecision on a model is holding me back right now. Gotta stick to one. Bias was bearish, which led me to wonder why i even took this long. Confluences were: 4H rejection wick CE, 15 min OB MT, 5 min OB MT, .79 OTE discount. Possible mistake 1. Using STDV, I had a level that price was heading to -4 before reversing, but remembering now, in a bearish trend, it usually never goes to -4. So my assumption that price will head to -4 and using that bias to create this trade probably was the root of the mistake. We were bearish, stdv doesn't hit 4 usually -2/2.5, and reverses, and i decided to long. Low probability now thinking back on this. Now I did see that price reacted well off the .7 golden zone, and used that to anticipate a .79 tap and retrace, but I now realize that that move was actually the retrace that the -2.5 range needed to do in order to short it to the -4 zone. {for the overall bearish stdv, not the internal stdv}. Now knowing this, I will be more aware of the true trend and what the story the stdv levels are telling me. Can always use entry triggers over limit orders for these types of retracements. Realistically, why tf would you long a bearish trend like that. THERE WAS ALSO AN SMT AT THE HIGHS, THAT'S HUGE INFO TO NOT LONG. (edited)

DAY 1:   1 trade 1 Loss. 

Technical Analysis
BIAS was bullish, though PA started off quite bearish to hunt for liquidity and imbalances. Because of that, I didn't expect price to move down as hard as it did. Realizing now that price is actually in between a range of two FVGs. This probably was a fault in the analysis. Realizing now the importance of the correct bias above all else to increase probability of winning trades. 

 Entered off of a 1 hour OB + 15 min OB + 5 min OB + 5 min swing OTE. Price REACTED and went for a 4R but ultimatly retraced and stopped me out. Mechanical issue is that i did not run my stop to BE after that, which cost me -100 of risk. That was the biggest mistake of the day. Did not follow my rule of SL at 3R. 

Psychological Analysis
I felt my heart beating a lot less than usual as I have more accepted the 100 risk as a loss before entered in. Even when I lost, there was a lot less negative emotion than last week. Actually glad that my level reacted the way it did, which gives me data to further use for my trades. The more I harp on the fact that this could have been a win or BE trade, the more emotional I get, so I am now accepting my loss as a mechanical one. There was an aspect of greed where i wanted price to shoot for swing high or 7.5 RR. And there was a psychological aspect of me not pulling my SL to BE. I wanted to believe that would just retest and get shot up, but because of that, I did not follow my rule and lost this trade. L risk management.  There was not much impulse to enter back in a trade which was great. Seems that now I'm more devoted to the process instead of the PNL. So the less I focus on the PNL, the better my psychology. If i think that i lost X amount of dollars, instead of focusing on what i did right, it will just tilt me. And that's not the right frame of thinking. I must focus on the strategy/game plan and rules. If these are followed, win/lose doesn't matter. It will pay off soon. (edited)

messages.content_text:
Day 3 - 18/05/26 (15m RB) (Win)


Getting onto the chart, I identified that Gold was bearish on the HTF, sweeping out some external lows and steadily rallying back up on the LTF
,


I marked a pretty clear 4H RB formed after sweeping these external lows. Overall I was wanting to see price trade into HTF imbalanced bearish price leg, but was confident that this RB would be mitigated in order to do that.
,


I dropped to the 15m and identified price had formed a really nice wick that contained engineered liquidity, and swept out equal highs swell which I saw as a pretty strong area that I could short from if the opportunity was there.
,

The other reason I saw this as a strong trade idea is because of the DOL’s and context provided.

Since the 02:00 4H candle had basically only traded to the buyside, it is fair to assume this bullish move is manipulation before a bearish move
,
The fact that there were super clear internal stacked lows on the way to this 02:00 level gives the trade more probability to play out quite clean as price generally likes to run these levels.
,


I set my LMT slightly below CE of the 15m RB with my SL above the high for 5 points, targeting the internal low before 02:00 for around 23 points and a 1:4.5RR. This was just incase price edged the level itself (it did, but 02:00 was met after a deeper rebalance of price).
,

Decent trade but was getting pretty uncomfortable with all of the chop around midnight open, especially after such a volatile selloff after I was filled. After Price displaced below midnight open I trailed my SL about 2 points in profit and had a break from watching the charts.
